papers.title_en: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
papers.evidence: 以持久会话级KV缓存作为个人助理的长期记忆
papers.tldr: 个人助手会积累数月对话，但现有长期记忆方案要在问题和证据之间做推导或选择，容易造成内容损失。KV-LTM 按会话同时存原始文本和固定读取模型下的 KV 缓存；回答时恢复缓存会话并追加问题。解析估算每 token 状态约 31K–328K 字节，30K token/日场景下每用户年 0.34–3.6 TB，而纯文本仅约 49 MB。文本是记录载体，缓存是免重算 prefill 加速器，可优雅退化为文本。
papers.abstract_en: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. We specify the design: storage record, budget-derived retention, append-only read path, and bounded aggregation. We size it analytically: across pinned BF16 full-attention (GQA) and latent-cached MLA configurations, per-token state spans approximately 31K-328K bytes (the pinned KDA+MLA hybrid differs: approximately 8.1K bytes/token plus a fixed per-session recurrent term), giving approximately 0.34-3.6 TB per user-year at a declared 30K-token/day scenario, against approximately 49 MB of raw text; per-query cost is modelled as regime-conditional transfer, attention, decode, aggregation, and compute. We define an evaluation protocol needing no persistent-cache implementation for logical QA evaluation: per-session prefill emulates valid cache reuse under the same model/input-state contract and ideal arithmetic, with named arms, controlled baselines, and a preregistered reader-model gate; a separate minimal real-cache replay tests numerical equivalence and measures the cost axis, with outcomes not assumed. KV-LTM trades storage for avoided re-prefill compute and write-time fidelity, within a declared retention budget.

papers.title_en: Semantic Context Handoff with On-Demand Evidence for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.authors: Guolong Zheng, Chen Hou, Xu Yang, Jianshan Zhang, Tao Huang
papers.evidence: 面向长程智能体的状态—证据分离与上下文记忆管理
papers.tldr: 传统长程LLM智能体用全历史提示交接上下文，成本随交互增长且可能损害准确率；仅保留压缩结论又会丢失后续有用证据。本文提出语义上下文交接SCH，将紧凑语义状态与可寻址的动作—观测证据分离，需要时按需回注且无需额外摘要或检索模型调用。在150项SWE-bench任务中，证据恢复将Pass@1从80.0%提升至86.9%，token与耗时基本不变；完整系统对比token少43%、墙钟时间少41%。该工作兼顾长程性能与上下文成本，并能从更早历史中恢复证据。
papers.abstract_en: Traditional long-horizon LLM agents often hand off context through full-history prompting, retaining all previous action--observation interactions. As execution proceeds, this history keeps growing, increasing inference cost and potentially degrading accuracy. Existing methods control this growth by preserving compact conclusions while removing earlier observations, but doing so can discard evidence that later becomes relevant. We introduce Semantic Context Handoff (SCH), whose central abstraction is state--evidence separation: a compact semantic state carries the agent's current interpretation, while supporting action--observation evidence remains separately addressable and can re-enter context when later execution makes it relevant, without separate summarization or retrieval-model calls.   Empirically, SCH improves long-horizon agent performance while substantially reducing context cost. In a controlled 150-task SWE-bench study, SCH's evidence recovery improves Pass@1 from $80.0\%$ to $86.9\%$ at essentially unchanged token use and execution time. In the complete-system comparison, SCH achieves 86.9% Pass@1 while using 43% fewer tokens and 41% less wall-clock time than the strongest baseline by task performance. Across models and benchmarks, SCH consistently reduces token use relative to full-history prompting while remaining competitive with or improving upon the evaluated baselines. Trajectory analysis confirms that SCH recovers evidence from substantially earlier parts of the interaction history rather than merely preserving a recent context window.

papers.title_en: Resolution as Attention for Efficient Agent Memory Perception
papers.authors: Siqi Xiang, Zhipeng Xu, Shengrui Liu, Zulong Chen, Chunyan Miao, Shijian Lu
papers.evidence: 面向智能体高效记忆管理的记忆感知机制
papers.tldr: 长程任务中LLM智能体积累大量交互历史，现有记忆管理多关注保留或检索什么，忽视对每条历史应分配多少感知细节。RAA将历史交互渲染为图像，并以视觉分辨率作为注意力分配手段，按与下一步决策的相关性动态调整分辨率。实验在多种任务与骨干模型上减少超50%视觉token消耗且不损任务表现。该方法可作为插件接入现有记忆管理，揭示自适应感知是智能体记忆的互补维度。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based agents accumulate extensive interaction histories when solving complex, long-horizon tasks, making efficient memory management critical to their performance and scalability. While existing memory management methods primarily focus on what to retain or retrieve, they often overlook how much perceptual detail should be allocated to individual past interactions. We posit that effective agent memory depends not only on the information preserved, but also on the granularity at which each past interaction is perceived. Motivated by this insight, we propose Resolution as Attention (RAA), a memory perception mechanism that uses visual resolution as a means of attention allocation across interaction histories. RAA renders past interactions as images and dynamically adjusts their resolution at every step according to their relevance to the agent's upcoming decision, preserving fine-grained information for critical interactions while reducing visual-token consumption for less relevant ones. To adaptively determine the perceptual fidelity of each interaction, we train a lightweight relevance estimator with teacher-model guidance and further optimize it to preserve the agent's decision consistency at a reduced visual-token cost. Experiments across multiple tasks and backbones show that RAA reduces token consumption by over 50% without compromising task performance. Moreover, RAA can be integrated as a plug-in perception layer with existing memory management methods, yielding further token savings and revealing adaptive perception as a complementary dimension of agent memory.

papers.title_en: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
papers.authors: Jiangyun Zhang, Zhou Tang, Kristen Surrao, Zhiyu Chen, Albert Guan, Tor Nitayanont, Yupei Zhang, Roopali Singh, Yunkai Xiao, Shreya Pandit, Julia Huang, Shayan Ali Akbar, Erwin Cornejo, Yuan Li, Yi Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向企业LLM智能体的自演化记忆架构
papers.tldr: 企业LLM智能体面临模型与流程快速变化，需兼顾准确率和成本。ARISE让记忆从自身失败中演化，将修正存为可检索微记忆并归纳为宏规则，仅在留出集准确率提升时接受规则。在14个企业工作流域、5个模型上，ARISE-Teacher较基线提升10.9/5.8个百分点，且优于GEPA；自归因版本仍提升10.0个百分点。贡献是无需更新权重、工具或流程逻辑的实用自演化记忆。
papers.abstract_en: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE uses the model itself or a teacher model to attribute the failures and propose corrections. Then, ARISE keeps the corrections as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out accuracy rises. Across 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and $τ^2$-bench using 5 models, ARISE-Teacher, which uses Claude Opus 4.6 for attribution and consolidation, gains 10.9 pp over the baseline on SOP-Bench and 5.8 pp on $τ^2$-bench. ARISE-Teacher also outperforms GEPA by 4.5 pp on $τ^2$-bench and 1.4 pp on SOP-Bench. With the deployment model as its own attributor, ARISE-Self still gains 10.0 pp on SOP-Bench. ARISE-Teacher uses 4.0% fewer model calls and 5.2% fewer output tokens at comparable per-task cost (-1.0%).

papers.title_en: KnowledgeClaw: Towards Agentic Knowledge Engineering via Omnimodal Hypergraphs
papers.authors: Haoran Luo, Jiapu Wang, Linhao Luo, Luu Anh Tuan
papers.evidence: 结合RAG与记忆智能体的知识工程
papers.tldr: 知识工程需把原始文件转为可推理知识库，但现有系统难以同时满足全模态、闭环生命周期与多粒度应用，且缺少统一评测。作者形式化OmniKE并发布OmniKE-Bench，包含六任务、1829个无模型条目和3960个真实文件。提出KnowledgeClaw，构建全模态类型化超图，用闭环生命周期智能体维护更新，并按查询路由到合适粒度。在30个基线中六项任务均第一，OKE达55.9，较最强基线高14.6。
papers.abstract_en: Knowledge engineering (KE) turns raw files into a reasoning-ready knowledge base, a task now within reach of LLM agents. KE has progressed from chunk and graph retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to memory agents, agentic KE and multimodal KE. However, a live knowledge base needs omnimodality, a closed-loop lifecycle and multi-granular application at once, yet existing systems meet at most two and no benchmark measures all three. We formalize Omnimodal Knowledge Engineering (OmniKE) and release OmniKE-Bench, six tasks with 1,829 model-free items over 3,960 real files in five modalities. We further propose KnowledgeClaw, an agentic system that builds an omnimodal typed hypergraph, keeps it current with a closed-loop lifecycle agent and routes each query to the granularity it needs. Against 30 baselines, it ranks first on all six tasks with an overall OKE of 55.9, +14.6 over the strongest baseline. Our software and data are publicly available at https://github.com/LHRLAB/KnowledgeClaw.

papers.title_en: MemoSync: Co-Managing Developer-Agent Metamemory Across Contexts
papers.authors: Baiqiao Zhang, Junze Li, Chunyang Luo, Yuying Tang, Wenshuo Zhang, Shiyuan Piao, Dingdong Liu, Shuai Ma, Xiaojuan Ma
papers.evidence: 面向智能体跨会话存储与检索的记忆系统
papers.tldr: AI编程代理跨会话与项目管理上下文，但开发者难以看清其存储、检索与应用，形成元记忆监控与控制断层。MemoSync将代理记忆建模为可共同操作的表征：代理提出候选并报告使用项，开发者审阅、编辑与限定范围。132人实验显示其任务表现显著更高、人机记忆对齐最佳，且主要源于监控准确性提升；更多操作未增加主观负荷，一周部署也融入日常开发。
papers.abstract_en: AI coding agents increasingly manage what context carries across sessions and projects, but developers have limited visibility into what these agents store, retrieve, and apply. This opacity creates a metamemory problem: the developer's meta-level judgments about what should be remembered are separated from the agent's object-level memory operations, disrupting the monitoring and control that keep the two levels aligned. We conducted a formative study with 12 developers and identified what they want to monitor and control across four dimensions of agent memory use. Based on these findings, we designed MemoSync, a co-management system that treats agent memory as a shared, operable representation: the agent proposes memory candidates and reports which items it uses, and the developer reviews, edits, and scopes them. In a between-subjects study (N=132) against two baselines, MemoSync participants achieved significantly higher task performance and the highest mean developer-agent memory alignment. In an exploratory mediation analysis, the alignment advantage was primarily driven by improved monitoring accuracy. Despite performing substantially more monitoring and control actions, participants reported no increase in perceived workload. A week-long deployment with nine developers showed that memory monitoring and control fit into everyday development work. MemoSync is open-sourced at https://github.com/SLEEPYBQ/MemoSync.
